title: Lehi speaks to Joseph
summary: Lehi addresses Joseph, recalls his birth in the wilderness, asks that the Lord consecrate the land to Joseph and his seed if they keep the commandments, and blesses Joseph, saying his seed will not be utterly destroyed.

explicit_facts.text: Lehi addresses Joseph, his last-born.
Joseph was born in the wilderness of Lehi's afflictions, and his mother bore him in the days of Lehi's greatest sorrow.
Lehi asks that the Lord consecrate the land for Joseph and his seed as an inheritance, conditional on keeping the commandments of the Holy One of Israel.
Lehi blesses Joseph and says his seed shall not utterly be destroyed.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Lehi addresses Joseph directly in a personal conversation.
unspecified_visual_details: The present conversation's location and circumstances are not stated.
Joseph's age, appearance, and posture are not stated.

spoken_dialogue.text: And now I speak unto you, Joseph, my last-born.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Lehi

narration.text: Thou wast born in the wilderness of mine afflictions;
may the Lord bless thee forever,

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Joseph's birth and Lehi's earlier afflictions are recalled, not depicted as present events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the birth as happening in the present scene.
Do not depict a divine appearance; the text does not describe one.

title: Joseph's lineage and covenant
summary: Lehi tells Joseph of his descent from Joseph who was carried captive into Egypt and recounts the promised branch and its future remembrance.

explicit_facts.text: Lehi says Joseph is the fruit of his loins and that Lehi is descended from Joseph who was carried captive into Egypt.
The Lord made covenants with Joseph; Lehi says Joseph saw their day and obtained a promise concerning a righteous branch from his lineage.
The branch would be remembered in the Lord's covenants and the Messiah would be made manifest to them in the latter days.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Lehi recounts these promises to Joseph as spoken teaching.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting and the appearance of the historical Joseph are unstated.

narration.text: And great were the covenants of the Lord which he made unto Joseph.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The branch, latter-day manifestation, and deliverance from darkness and captivity are prophetic teaching, not narrated present events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Joseph in Egypt, the branch, or a visible Messiah.

title: Promise of a choice seer
summary: Lehi recounts Joseph's prophecy that the Lord would raise a choice seer from his descendants and give him a commanded work for his brethren.

explicit_facts.text: Joseph testified that the Lord would raise up a choice seer from the fruit of his loins.
The seer would be esteemed among Joseph's descendants, receive a commandment, and do work of great worth by bringing his brethren to knowledge of the covenants.
The seer would do no other work than what the Lord commanded and would do the Lord's work.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Lehi recounts Joseph's prophecy while addressing Joseph.
unspecified_visual_details: The identity and appearance of the seer are not stated here.

narration.text: A seer shall the Lord my God raise up,

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The seer and his future work are described prophetically, not shown as present events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show the seer performing future work.

title: The seer and Moses
summary: Lehi's quoted prophecy compares the future seer to Moses and foretells Moses delivering the people from Egypt and the seer bringing forth and confirming the Lord's word.

explicit_facts.text: The seer would be great like Moses, whom the Lord would raise up to deliver Israel.
Moses would be raised up to deliver the people from Egypt.
A seer from Joseph's descendants would have power to bring forth the Lord's word and convince them of the word already gone forth among them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Lehi continues delivering prophetic teaching to Joseph.
unspecified_visual_details: No appearance is described for Moses or the future seer.

narration.text: And he shall be great like unto Moses,
Moses will I raise up, to deliver thy people out of the land of Egypt.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The future deliverance and seer's work are prophecy, not present action.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Moses, Egypt, or the seer as present in the scene.

title: Two writings grow together
summary: Lehi recounts the prophecy that writings from Joseph's descendants and Judah will grow together, establish peace, and aid restoration; the seer will be made strong from weakness.

explicit_facts.text: Joseph's descendants and Judah's descendants would write, and their writings would grow together.
The writings would confound false doctrines, lay down contentions, establish peace, and bring knowledge of the fathers and covenants in the latter days.
The seer would be made strong out of weakness when the Lord's work commenced among his people, unto restoration of Israel.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Lehi delivers this prophecy as spoken teaching.
unspecified_visual_details: The writers, documents, and future restoration are not shown or visually described.

narration.text: out of weakness he shall be made strong,

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The writings growing together and the strength from weakness are prophetic language; do not literalize them as a visible supernatural event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent written documents, a future seer, or a gathering scene.

title: Joseph's confidence in the promise
summary: Lehi quotes Joseph's confidence that the seer will be blessed, bear a name connected to Joseph and his father, and help bring his people to salvation; the Lord will preserve Joseph's seed.

explicit_facts.text: Joseph prophesied that the Lord would bless the seer and confound those who seek to destroy him.
The seer would be named after Joseph and after his father, and the Lord would bring his people to salvation by the seer's hand.
Joseph expressed confidence in the promise of Moses and said the Lord would preserve his seed forever.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Lehi recounts Joseph's words while speaking to his son.
unspecified_visual_details: The seer, his father, and the threatened opponents are not visually described.

narration.text: Behold, I am sure of the fulfilling of this promise;
I will preserve thy seed forever.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The seer's future danger and salvation are prophetic, not present events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict an attack on the seer or a visible divine intervention.

title: Moses and a spokesman
summary: Lehi recounts the Lord's words concerning Moses receiving power in a rod and law in writing, with a spokesman, and a future descendant who writes with a spokesman to declare it.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord would raise up Moses, give him power in a rod and judgment in writing, and write his law by his own hand; Moses would have a spokesman.
The Lord would raise up one from Joseph's descendants, provide him a spokesman, and have him write the writing of Joseph's descendants for them to receive.
The spokesman of that descendant would declare the writing.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Lehi recounts the prophecy as teaching, without staging its future events.
unspecified_visual_details: The descendant, both spokesmen, the rod, and the writing are not visually described in this present scene.

narration.text: I will make a spokesman for him.
the spokesman of thy loins shall declare it.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These are prophetic statements rather than present-tense visible events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Lord's hand writing or invent the identities or appearances of either spokesman.

title: Words from the dust
summary: Lehi recounts the prophecy that the descendants' written words will reach their brethren after generations and call them to repentance; the Lord will strengthen their words through faith.

explicit_facts.text: The writing would contain words the Lord deemed expedient to go forth to Joseph's descendants and be as though they cried to them from the dust.
After many generations, their cry would go to their brethren, including a call to repentance, in the simpleness of their words.
Because of their faith, their words would proceed from the Lord and be made strong, leading to remembrance of the covenant.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Lehi continues teaching Joseph about the future written words.
unspecified_visual_details: The generations, written words, and dust are not described as a literal visible scene.

narration.text: And it shall be as if the fruit of thy loins had cried unto them from the dust;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: “Cried unto them from the dust” is figurative teaching about written words, not a literal appearance or voice from the dead.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the dead speaking or a supernatural voice rising from dust.

title: Lehi applies the prophecy to Joseph
summary: Lehi tells Joseph that his father of old prophesied in this manner and blesses him under the covenant, saying his seed will not be destroyed because they will heed the book's words.

explicit_facts.text: Lehi tells Joseph that his father of old prophesied in this manner.
Lehi says Joseph is blessed because of the covenant and his seed will not be destroyed, for they will hearken to the words of the book.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Lehi directly addresses Joseph in applying the prophecy to him.
unspecified_visual_details: The book and the setting of the conversation are not described.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The future response to the book is prophesied, not shown as a present event.

title: A mighty instrument
summary: Lehi foretells one mighty among Joseph's descendants who will do good in word and deed as an instrument of God and bring restoration to Israel and Joseph's brethren's seed.

explicit_facts.text: One mighty would rise among Joseph's descendants and do much good in word and deed as an instrument in God's hands, with exceeding faith.
He would work mighty wonders and bring much restoration to the house of Israel and the seed of Joseph's brethren.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Lehi presents this as a prophecy to Joseph.
unspecified_visual_details: The mighty person's identity and appearance are not supplied in this verse.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This future figure and his deeds are prophesied, not shown in a present-tense scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show wonders or identify the person beyond what the supplied text says.

title: Lehi's final counsel to Joseph
summary: Lehi blesses Joseph, calls him little, counsels him to heed Nephi's words and remember his dying father, and concludes.

explicit_facts.text: Lehi blesses Joseph and says he is little.
Lehi tells Joseph to hearken to Nephi's words and remember his dying father.
Lehi concludes with “Amen.”

reasonable_visual_inferences: Lehi speaks a closing blessing and counsel directly to Joseph.
unspecified_visual_details: Joseph's age and the precise setting are unstated.
